title: Brake Pad Replacement
summary: Blueprint for inspecting brake pads, rotors, calipers, and hardware before quoting a pad-only or pads-and-rotors repair.
symptoms: Squeal, grind, or scraping while braking
Brake warning light or low pad sensor message
Longer stopping distance or brake pulsation
Uneven pad wear side to side
inspect_first: Inner and outer pad thickness on both sides
Rotor surface, thickness, scoring, and runout clues
Caliper slide pin movement and boot condition
Brake fluid level and visible hose or caliper leaks
likely_causes: Sticking slide pins or seized hardware
Rotor damage or excessive heat spots
repair_overview: Measure pads and inspect rotors before quoting the final path.
Remove caliper hardware, support the caliper, and replace pads and clips.
Service slide pins and contact points with proper brake lubricant.
Pump the pedal, verify pedal feel, and road test carefully.
common_mistakes: Replacing pads without inspecting rotor condition
Letting the caliper hang from the brake hose
Driving before restoring brake pedal feel
estimate_guidance: Use pad-only pricing only when rotors, calipers, and hardware pass inspection.
Quote pads and rotors when scoring, pulsation, rust lip, or thickness concerns are present.
Add caliper or brake-fluid service only when inspection supports it.

recommended_repairs.title: Rotor Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Commonly checked with pad work when rotors are scored, warped, thin, or heat damaged.

recommended_repairs.title: Brake Fluid Service
recommended_repairs.description: Consider when fluid is dark, contaminated, or service history is unknown.

recommended_repairs.title: Caliper Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Mechanics often inspect calipers when pad wear is uneven or the wheel shows drag after braking.

diagnostic_context.intro: Brake noise and uneven wear should be inspected before choosing pad-only versus pads-and-rotors pricing.
